concerns.text: FR-005 explicitly forbids 'arbitrary sine/cosine terms based on log n' and mandates only 'theoretically motivated' density features. Tasks T016a and T017a mandate the inclusion of sin(log n) and cos(log n) as predictors, directly violating the functional requirement and the Constitution Principle VII (Density-Dependent Correlation Rigor).

The Plan's 'Complexity Tracking' section and the nature of residual data (autocorrelated) require 'Time-Series CV (blocking)'. Task T024 explicitly implements 'scikit-learn's KFold' (standard random partitioning), which violates the statistical validity required by SC-002 and the Plan's own methodology constraints.

FR-001 and T016a require calculating 'prime_gap_size' for n near the upper bound (50,000), which necessitates access to the 'next prime' > 50,000. Task T004 limits the sieve to exactly 50,000 without a documented overflow strategy or fallback to generate the next prime, violating the data hygiene and feature engineering requirements.

Constitution Principle VI requires explicit reporting of the residual error term for the finite n range. Task T038 creates the artifact but lacks specific content requirements (e.g., explicit reporting of the error term methodology), making the 'measurable' aspect of the constitution check untestable and the task scope insufficient.

FR-002 mandates explicit validation of Meinardus' theorem conditions (pole structure) and a fallback to truncated Dirichlet series if conditions are not met. Tasks T005 and T041 focus on implementation and documentation but lack a specific task to implement the validation logic and the fallback mechanism, violating the functional requirement.
